title: Persist the stranded implementation lane's merged state so its stale scope lock is released, without claiming Done

sha_binding.verified_source_note: The last non-proof commit on this branch: the single canonical record-merge write this bundle describes. It is the anchor only because a file cannot contain its own SHA; post-merge rebinding sets merge_sha. merge_sha is explicitly null pre-merge rather than a branch SHA or a placeholder.

premise_check.claim: The predecessor lane's file_scope_lock is held solely because its manifest status is in_review, which is a member of ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES; recording the merge that actually happened moves it to merged, which is not, and that alone releases the lock.
premise_check.method: Read ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES and the TRANSITIONS table in scripts/ops/shared.ts. Reproduced the admission refusal by executing ops:lane-start for the successor repair lane. Read the post-merge refusal in scripts/ops/scope-release.ts. Read the merge facts from the GitHub API, not from any manifest.
premise_check.result: Confirmed. ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES = {started, in_progress, in_review, blocked, parked, reopened} — merged is absent. TRANSITIONS lists in_review -> merged. The admission refusal reproduced with code file_scope_conflict on exactly scripts/ops/proof-schema.ts and scripts/ops/proof-schema.test.ts.

alternatives_rejected.blocked_or_parked: Both are members of ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES, so neither releases the lock; the conflict would be byte-identical and the record less true.
alternatives_rejected.widen_scope_release: scope-release refuses on a non-OPEN PR by design (scripts/ops/scope-release.ts:222-224). Those paths were genuinely modified by the merged PR, so releasing them post-merge would change what the safety mechanism means. Not authorized and not attempted.
alternatives_rejected.reopen_as_multi_pr_lane: Rejected: the predecessor's implementation is merged; reopening would misrepresent it as in flight.

mutation_testing.reason: This lane adds no control and changes no code. Its entire functional content is one canonical-command-produced state record. There is no guard here whose failure condition could be inverted. The controls this record relies on — ACTIVE_LOCK_STATUSES membership, the TRANSITIONS table, and record-merge's refusal to fabricate a truth-check receipt — are pre-existing and owned by other lanes; each was verified by reading source and by observing the command's actual output rather than by asserting it.
mutation_testing.negative_observation_recorded: The admission conflict was reproduced by execution before this lane existed (code file_scope_conflict, overlapping_files exactly the two proof-schema paths). That is the failing condition this record is meant to clear, and it must be observed to clear after merge; if it does not, this lane's premise is wrong and that must be reported rather than overridden.

static_proof.verify_full: PARTIAL - every static stage PASSES; test:live-db refuses locally because ci:assert-staging reports host=127.0.0.1 ref=unidentified expected=xskgrzbteyqdufktjrjx. This lane's proof profile is static: it touches no DB surface, issues no query, and changes no runtime behaviour. No live-DB claim is made.
static_proof.lane_suites_note: This lane changes no source file, so it has no owning test suite. The full static suite was run in place of a targeted one.

safety_posture.runtime_behaviour_change: none — one lane manifest state record
safety_posture.other_lane_manifests_edited: exactly one, docs/06_status/lanes/UTV2-1729.json, which is this lane's authorized target and the sole functional change
safety_posture.note: This lane records a merge that already happened. It does not close a lane, does not certify a lane Done, and does not repair the defect that stranded it.

known_gaps: No Codex invocation occurred. The lane is registered executor codex-cli, but the entire authorized implementation is one canonical command with no authored code, so it was run directly. The model-routing sidecar declares the lane's registered routing and deliberately omits codex_exit_code and codex_cli_version, which would assert a run that did not happen. Disclosed rather than papered over; re-registering the lane as Claude-executed is a PM call.

This unblocks admission; it does not prove the successor repair correct. After this lands, the repair lane's ops:lane-start must be re-attempted and observed to succeed. If the predecessor still appears as a file_scope_conflict, this lane's premise is wrong and that must be reported, not overridden.

The predecessor is left in a state no automation will advance on its own. merged releases the lock but its closeout still fails on P10/R3, so it is reachable only by an explicit sanctioned closeout replay after the repair lands. Intended, but the record will sit visibly incomplete in the interim and nothing will nag about it.

scope-release remains unusable post-merge. This lane routes around that rather than fixing it, so any future lane whose closeout fails after merge hits the same cycle and needs the same bridge. Widening scope-release was considered and explicitly rejected as a change to the safety mechanism's meaning.

The root control checkout carries untracked shadow copies of the predecessor's manifest and .ops/sync file that disagree with main (they read 'started'). They are not repository truth, they blocked git pull --ff-only, and one early read in this session came from the shadow before the discrepancy was caught. They are preserved unmodified outside the repository pending separate classification; this lane neither restores nor deletes them.

sign_off.note: This bundle is evidence, not certification. The done-gate is ops:truth-check, and T1 authority is PM's.
